name: Worldviews and Ultimate Authorities

objectives.text: Identify the Bible as God's Word that tells us what is true
Explain that God decides what is true and right because He made everything and owns everything
Identify that people believe different things about who made the world and who is in charge of it
Describe a worldview as the set of beliefs a person uses to understand everything, using the picture of looking through glasses
Explain from Scripture that every person trusts something as a final authority, either God or something in creation such as the self
Identify the big worldview questions of origin, meaning, morality, and destiny and state the Bible's answer to each
Compare the biblical account of human origin and purpose with a naturalistic account that sees people as products of chance
Explain the Reformed teaching that Scripture is to be believed on the authority of God its author rather than on the testimony of any person or church
Use Scripture as the standard to test a claim heard in everyday life or media
Define a presupposition and identify the presuppositions underlying sample statements and arguments
Explain from Scripture why the Reformed tradition holds that no one reasons from a neutral standpoint
Explain how Proverbs 1:7 and Colossians 2:3 present the fear of the Lord as the starting point of true knowledge
Explain from Romans 1 why the Reformed tradition teaches that evidence alone does not persuade unbelievers who know God yet suppress the truth
Explain how the distinction between Creator and creature makes God's word the final authority over human reasoning
Explain why an ultimate authority cannot be proven by appeal to any higher authority, using God swearing by Himself as an example
Construct a diagram that traces a chain of justification for a belief back to the ultimate authority it rests on
Analyze a contemporary cultural work to identify its underlying worldview and the ultimate authority it assumes
Classify major philosophical positions such as rationalism, empiricism, and autonomous individualism by the ultimate authority each assumes
Compare the presuppositional approach to the authority of Scripture with classical and evidential apologetic approaches regarding where reasoning begins
Evaluate the charge of circular reasoning by distinguishing vicious circularity from the unavoidable circularity of any ultimate authority

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (worldview definition, everyone trusts some authority, Christian versus secular origins, presuppositions, myth of neutrality, fear of the Lord, Romans 1 suppression, ultimate authority diagram, circular reasoning). Dropped vague or filler items (observing that some do not believe the Bible, applying the Bible as starting point without a task) and replaced childish wording such as boss of truth. Moved the failure of empiricism and rationalism and the necessity of the Christian worldview to the Internal Critique and TAG siblings, keeping only classification of authorities here. Added the self-authenticating authority of Scripture, testing claims by Scripture, the big worldview questions, the Creator-creature distinction, cultural worldview analysis, and comparison with other apologetic methods. Anchored objectives to specific verses and to Westminster Confession 1.4, 1.5, 1.10, 2.2 and Shorter Catechism Q1 and Q10 where they state the doctrine.
